summary: Autopilot enrollment failing during provisioning due to provisioning-VLAN ACL blocking Microsoft endpoints
description:
Issue summary: Multiple new corporate workstations fail Azure AD / Autopilot enrollment during automated provisioning. Devices complete imaging but show as 'Not Joined' in Intune and reach a local account OOBE state. Impact: Blocks batch onboarding for a new cohort of hires; prevents BitLocker key escrow and standard policy application. Scope observed on 12 devices across 2 imaging racks; appears correlated to devices booting on the 'provisioning' VLAN.

Observed behavior:
- Device applies OS image and reboots to OOBE.
- Windows shows 'Can't connect to your organization' or times out on the 'Sign in with work or school account' stage.
- Devices end up with a locally created admin account (autopilot fallback) and do not appear in AAD as Hybrid/AAD joined.

Initial hypothesis: Intune/Azure endpoints are being blocked or timed out during enrollment when devices are on the provisioning VLAN, causing autopilot service calls to fail and fallback to local provisioning flow.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Boot device in imaging rack connected to provisioning VLAN.
2) Start Windows Autopilot provisioning with latest corp image.
3) Observe network calls to Microsoft/Graph endpoints during OOBE enrollment stage.
4) After timeout, device falls back to local account creation.
5) Check Intune device list and Autopilot service logs for failed enrollments.
investigation_notes:
- Collected network packet capture from an affected rack (pcap saved to /shared/logs/pcaps/INT-87245_provisioning.pcap).
- Observed repeated TCP RSTs and SYN timeouts to graph.microsoft.com and login.microsoftonline.com from devices on provisioning VLAN only.
- Firewall and layer-3 ACLs for the provisioning VLAN were recently updated (change committed 2026-03-09) - commit ID referenced in infra PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-config/pull/842.
- ACL rules shown to inadvertently block outbound 443 to a subset of Microsoft IP ranges (customer-requested hardening for lab segmentation).
- Devices on corporate workstation VLAN (non-provisioning) do not show the issue.
- Intune logs on the service side show failed enrollment attempts with timeout errors; local device logs (eventvwr) show MDM enrollment timeouts and AAD join error 0x801c0003.
- No evidence of incorrect image or driver failure; token acquisition reached a TLS handshake but then connection reset.
- SRE confirmed ACL change rolled out to provisioning VLAN switches at 2026-03-09 04:12 UTC.
comments: Aisha Patel (Reporter) [2026-03-10]: Noted first reports from hiring ops: 6 devices failed this morning in rack B3. Raising to SRE as P1 because onboarding blocked.
Marco Alvarez (Assignee) [2026-03-10]: Investigating network captures. Reached out to SRE network on #infra-networking. Will attach pcap and look for dropped connections.

SRE-Network (SRE) [2026-03-11]: Confirmed ACL change on provisioning VLAN that restricts outbound IP ranges. We see denied packets to Microsoft Graph endpoints. Rolling back ACL on the provisioning VLAN will restore connectivity.

Marco Alvarez [2026-03-11]: Performed controlled rollback for rack B3 and re-ran provisioning on 3 test units — all 3 successfully enrolled and appeared in Intune. Marking as actionable fix; need full VLAN rollback and runbook update.

Security (InfoSec) [2026-03-12]: We understand ACL intended to reduce exposure in lab. Recommend adding explicit allow rules for Microsoft enrollment ranges and document exceptions. Will review change flow to require an impact assessment for provisioning VLAN changes.
Marco Alvarez [2026-03-13]: Coordinating full rollback with SRE. Also creating alert to detect enrollment timeouts during autopilot runs to catch regressions early.
resolution:
Temporary fix: Rolled back the restrictive ACL on provisioning VLAN for all imaging racks (completed 2026-03-12). Verified by repro on 10 affected devices — successful Autopilot enrollment, BitLocker escrow and policy application.
Permanent remediation: Update infra-config repo to add explicit allow rules for Intune/Autopilot and Graph endpoints before re-applying segmentation rules (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-config/pull/843). Update provisioning runbook to include network impact checklist and require automated enrollment smoke test post-change.
Post-incident actions:
- Runbook updated at https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/autopilot-provisioning-runbook (section "Network change checklist").
- Create monitoring alert to fire when >5 Autopilot enrollments fail within 30 minutes in any rack (ticket INT-87246 created to track alerting work).
follow_up_tasks: INT-87246 - Implement autopilot enrollment failure alerting
Infra PR 843 - Add explicit allow list for enrollment endpoints and document exceptions
Schedule post-change review with InfoSec and SRE (owner: Marco Alvarez)
